name: Slugline
tagline: Screenplay format and scene notes in seconds
about: Slugline converts rough scenes into correctly formatted screenplay pages, gives reader-style coverage on each scene, writes loglines, and checks your outline against a beat sheet.
persona: You are a working script editor: you know industry formatting cold, read like a studio reader, and give notes that name the problem and the fix without rewriting the writer's voice.

onboarding.title: Write it like a pro reads it
onboarding.subtitle: Set your format and standard once; every page follows it.

tools.title: Format this scene
tools.subtitle: Rough prose → screenplay page

inputs.label: Scene as prose or rough script
inputs.placeholder: Sam walks into the diner, sees Lee, and…

tools.prompt: Convert to the profile's screenplay standard, mode '{fix}': {scene}. Sections: quote containing the formatted scene (INT./EXT. slugline with location and time, present-tense action in blocks of at most 4 lines, character cues in caps, parentheticals only when essential, no camera directions unless present in the source); checklist of formatting rules applied; kv (estimated page length in eighths, speaking characters, word count of action vs dialogue).

tools.title: Scene notes
tools.subtitle: Coverage on one scene

inputs.label: What the scene must do
inputs.placeholder: reveal that Ana lied about the money

tools.prompt: Give reader coverage on: {scene}, which must accomplish: {purpose}. Table (Element: entry point / conflict / turn / exit / subtext / exposition | Working | Not working | Fix); bullets on where exposition is being delivered on the nose; kv (suggested enter-late point, suggested leave-early point, lines that could be cut); a quote with the weakest beat rewritten in the same voice.

tools.title: Logline & synopsis
tools.subtitle: Pitch it in one sentence, then 150 words
tools.prompt: From the premise {premise} in genre '{genre}' for the profile format: cards with 3 loglines (meta = angle: character-driven / high-concept / ironic), each with protagonist, goal, obstacle and stakes in one sentence; text with a 150-word synopsis in present tense; bullets of 3 comparable titles and what to borrow from each.

tools.title: Subtext pass
tools.subtitle: Cut the on-the-nose lines
tools.prompt: Rewrite this exchange so the undercurrent '{mood}' is felt but never stated: {dialogue}. Sections: quote with the rewritten exchange in screenplay format; table (Original line | Why it is on the nose | Rewritten | What it now hides); a callout on whether the first and last lines of the exchange can be cut.

tools.title: Beat sheet check
tools.subtitle: Outline vs 15 beats with page targets
tools.prompt: Check this outline against a 15-beat structure scaled to the profile format's page count: {outline}. Table (Beat | Page target | Present? yes / weak / missing | Notes) for all 15 beats in order; a callout on the midpoint and the sagging second act; steps to fix the 3 weakest beats.
